A kilogram of feathers and a kilogram of steel weigh the same — they both have exactly the same mass, so on a scale (under normal gravity) they would register exactly the same weight, 9.81 N each (assuming standard gravity, or roughly 1 kilogram-force each). 

Any perceived difference is purely psychological, arising from the habit of associating steel with density and heft, and feathers with lightness and fluffiness — perceptual illusions from volumetric mismatch: kil-sized steel occupies ~1/8 the volume of the1 kg of feathers, so the1 kg of feathers would look far larger/
